claim_being_bridged: That a Rigvedic lemma Turner marks with a Dravidian arrow records contact between Indo-Aryan and Dravidian speakers.
tested_here: Partly. The lemma's presence and its stratum are measured (DE-M-009 to DE-M-012); the etymology is Turner's, not this record's.
notes: A dictionary's attribution and a historical contact event are two things. Turner's bracket is a judgement made in the 1960s, resting in 36% of cases on Burrow and in 38% on Mayrhofer (DE-M-030). To cross this bridge the etymologies must be checked individually against DEDR and against Indo-Aryan-internal alternatives - the null, HYP-E-000. That work is not done here.

claim_being_bridged: That loan candidates clustering in Arnold's Popular stratum shows the borrowing happened late in the Rigvedic period.
tested_here: The clustering is measured: 10 of 21 tokens, against a 13.9% baseline (DE-M-012).
verdict: WEAK - THREE SEPARATE FAILURES OF INDEPENDENCE
notes: First, the strata are Arnold 1905 and nothing else (DEP-001). Second, Popular stratum and book 10 are not independent instruments (DEP-004), so a book-order confirmation would be circular. Third, a metrical stratum is a compositional layer, not a calendar. And the candidate set is 15 lemmas. The measurement stands; this inference does not follow from it without work not done here.

claim_being_bridged: That where Dravidian and Munda languages are recorded now constrains where they were three thousand years ago.
tested_here: The modern distribution is measured (DE-M-021 to DE-M-025).
notes: Constitution §4.P forbids converting modern areal distribution automatically into prehistoric substrate. The measurement is a starting point for the geography gate and never its conclusion. Brahui is the standing demonstration that the modern map understates the past distribution of at least one family - which is why HYP-E-002's geography verdict is 'adverse' and not 'fails'.

claim_being_bridged: That Dravidian or Munda speech implies a distinct ancestry, and that ancestry results speak to language.
tested_here: No. No genetic evidence was retrieved or used in this unit.
notes: Constitution §4.E: genetic admixture dates for present-day Munda-speaking populations constrain demographic models but do not directly date or exclude a language. IH-112 and IH-119 carry ancestry claims at INHERITED-UNVERIFIED and none of them is used here. This unit is lexical and geographic only.

link_from: a substrate donor in the northwest
link_to: the language of the Indus civilisation
claim_being_bridged: That establishing a Dravidian presence in the northwest supports a Dravidian reading of the Indus script.
notes: Two separate claims. HYP-E-001 passing its gate says nothing about HYP-E-008, which is deferred out of scope. The site's existing position (IH-136, IH-118) is untouched by this unit and stays INHERITED-UNVERIFIED.

claim_being_bridged: That an arrow in CDIAL means the etymology is accepted in the field today.
tested_here: Partly: hedging is counted (DE-M-005) and the cited authority is counted (DE-M-028 to DE-M-030).
notes: CDIAL was compiled 1962-66. Constitution step 11 requires current standing to be established separately, and nothing retrieved here establishes it: Mayrhofer's EWA, which Turner cites in 85 cases, was not retrieved, and neither was any post-1990 assessment. What is in the register is Turner's judgement with its date attached, and that is all it is offered as.

claim_being_bridged: That a starred Proto-Dravidian form can stand in evidence beside a Rigvedic lemma.
tested_here: The two are held in separate tables and separate registers throughout (DE-M-013 against DE-M-014).
notes: Constitution §4.E's attestation gradient. DEDR offers no reconstructions at all, which is why distinctions 1 and 2 required separate sources here: the reflexes come from SRC-061 and the starred forms from SRC-062. Nothing in this unit lets a starred form supply attestation.

claim_being_bridged: That a word appearing only inside Rigvedic compounds counts as attested in the Rigveda.
tested_here: Yes - measured and separated into three columns (DE-M-020).
verdict: REFUSED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS PRODUCTIVE
notes: kunda and mayura have no Rigvedic simplex but do occur in compounds, and Turner says so himself. Merging the two would have added them to the simplex count; treating compound absence as total absence would have lost them. Both errors were available and both are avoided by keeping three columns. The columns are string matches and need case-by-case review: of the four raised, two are real and two (*garda to gardabha-, pota to potar-) are spelling coincidences.

claim_being_bridged: That the Indus signs encode speech, so that counting them, sequencing them and comparing them is linguistics rather than iconography.
tested_here: No. Nothing retrieved bears on it.
notes: This is the bridge the English word 'script' crosses silently, which is why this record does not use it of the object (06-BRIEFS/domain-k-translation-blocks.md §4). Registered at DK-H-001 and its complement DK-H-011, both gated NOT-ELIGIBLE-SOURCE-BLOCKED.

claim_being_bridged: That an object which makes an impression was used to authenticate, control or account for goods on behalf of an institution.
tested_here: No. The retrieved objects carry no find-spot, no context and no associated sealing (DK-M-016, DK-M-018).
notes: Two separate claims are folded into one word: that the object was used to seal, and that the sealing served an institution. The first is a use claim testable from impressions and wear; the second is a social claim testable from context. Neither was testable here. DK-H-003, DK-H-004.

link_from: the person who cut a seal
claim_being_bridged: That the maker and the user of a seal are the same person, or belong to the same group, so that a statement about 'seal owners' covers both.
tested_here: No, and it cannot be from this data.
notes: The reason this record says sign-makers and sign-users as two terms. Craft production and institutional use are different positions and the surviving record was not made to document the first (DK-A-012, constitution §4.V).

link_to: the end of the institutions the signs served
claim_being_bridged: That when the signs stop appearing, the institutions that used them had ended.
tested_here: No. Nothing about the end of sign use was retrieved (DK-A-009).
notes: The bridge can fail in both directions: a practice can outlive its institution on other media, and an institution can outlive the practice by changing medium. Either failure breaks the packet's own framing at DK-H-006.

claim_being_bridged: That because the seals, the sign system and the urban form ended, the people ended too.
tested_here: Yes, and it fails on its own terms.
notes: §4.K names this as the trap. The inference is invalid independently of any evidence: institutions end while the people who lived under them continue. DK-H-009 records it as REJECTED and the row is kept permanently visible so it is not re-proposed.

link_from: the absence of writing vocabulary in the Rigveda
link_to: the absence of writing from the world the Rigveda's composers lived in
claim_being_bridged: That because the corpus has no word for writing, nobody in reach of its composers wrote.
tested_here: Yes. The lexical absence is measured (DK-R-002, DK-R-003) and the bridge is refused.
notes: A liturgical praise corpus records what the liturgy and the patron need. The archive audit at APA-K-001 says what such a corpus would and would not record; DK-H-010 registers the genre explanation as the null. The measurement is strong and the inference from it is weak, and the two must not be quoted together.

link_from: a proposed reading of the Indus signs
link_to: a modern linguistic community and its claims
claim_being_bridged: That identifying the sign system's language would identify whose ancestors made it, and thereby settle a modern question of priority.
notes: Three separate bridges in one move: signs to language, language to population, ancient population to modern identity. Constitution §4.E's attestation gradient and step 10 both forbid crossing them silently. This record registers the one retrieved decipherment claim at DK-H-007 and rejects it on recoverability, not on its linguistic politics.

claim_being_bridged: That 179 objects, 984 sign tokens, 181 sign classes and a median length of 5 describe the Indus material.
tested_here: Yes. Measured and refused in every row of the measurement register.
notes: The sample is one object class - unicorn seals - at one site, selected by one annotator, from a catalogue this session cannot open (DK-M-002, DK-M-003, DEP-029). The counts are true of the file and of nothing else.

link_from: an iconographic class on a seal
link_to: a social class, office or institution
claim_being_bridged: That the unicorn seals mark a group - merchants, an elite, a clan - so that their frequency measures that group.
tested_here: No. It could not be: the retrieved sample contains only unicorn seals, so within it the class has no contrast to measure against.
notes: Recorded because the retrieved sample invites exactly this reading and is incapable of supporting it. A frequency needs a denominator, and this file has none.

claim_being_bridged: That the Rigvedic occurrences can be read through the later sense, or that the later sense shows the Rigvedic one already implied writing.
tested_here: Half of it. The Rigvedic sense is measured across all 8 occurrences (DK-R-008); the later development is not evidenced here at all.
notes: The direction matters. Reading the later sense backwards manufactures Rigvedic literacy; reading the Rigvedic sense forwards would deny a development that certainly happened. Neither is done. Dating and evidencing the development needs sources that are blocked - HOLD-008.
